subject.title: fix(infra): make exec-approvals lock ownership filesystem-safe

question: Which current-main branch should be the canonical fix for the exec-approvals VirtioFS lock leak, and should it be accepted only after exact-head live filesystem proof?
rationale: Both open PRs claim the same security-sensitive lock correction, while neither is merged and this rebased branch does not yet provide inspectable runtime evidence for its latest head.

options.title: Verify this rebase, then keep it canonical
options.body: Require a redacted exact-head VirtioFS run covering release, unrelated contention, and same-process reentrancy before selecting this rebased PR as the landing candidate.

options.title: Continue with the original proposal
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 as the canonical candidate if maintainers prefer its existing live-redeploy evidence and can rebase it safely.

options.title: Pause both implementations
options.body: Defer landing until an owner validates the lock contract and decides whether the shared dependency or this owner-local implementation is the durable boundary.

recommendation.title: Verify this rebase, then keep it canonical
recommendation.body: Require a redacted exact-head VirtioFS run covering release, unrelated contention, and same-process reentrancy before selecting this rebased PR as the landing candidate.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the current production reproduction and authored the related implementation that this PR rebases.
